citation: docs/architecture.md, durability: what can be written down is written down, and a live process cannot be. The rule that a saved region is a wish checked against the daemon follows from the same section - a daemon restart returns the pane tree and each pane's directory but not the processes, so a tab named here may or may not still exist.
why: Reopening is where a saved arrangement meets a session that moved on while the app was closed. Everything in it is intent - the tabs somebody had, which was on screen, how wide each machine's half of one was - and none of it is a claim that any of it still exists. So the decision worth pinning is which of it survives the check and which tab the window opens onto, because both failure modes are silent: a tab kept for a session nobody holds renders a caption that goes nowhere, and a window that opens showing nothing ignores the keyboard without saying why.

cases.name: everything is still there
cases.why: The ordinary reopen, and the one that has to keep order and widths exactly: a window that comes back with its regions shuffled or evened out is one somebody has to rearrange every morning.

cases.name: a tab that is gone leaves the window
cases.why: A tab nobody holds any more renders as a caption that goes nowhere and a square that never fills in. The check is against what each daemon turns out to hold, because a saved tab is a wish and the session moved on while the app was closed.

cases.name: the window comes back on the tab it was showing
cases.why: The arrangement records which tab was on screen, and it survives the tabs around it disappearing. This is the thing a person notices: coming back to the work they left rather than to whatever happens to be first.

cases.name: the tab that was on screen is the one that went
cases.why: The window has to open onto something. The first survivor rather than nothing at all - a window with tabs in it and none on screen ignores the keyboard and cannot say why.

cases.name: a machine that is not there takes its half of every tab
cases.why: A tab spanning two machines opens on the half it can reach rather than refusing, which is the rule the mirror already follows for a stale daemon applied to a tab (MIP-2, durability). The regions that go are that machine's; the tab stays if anything is left of it, and goes when nothing is.

cases.name: nothing survives, and the window opens as a first launch does
cases.why: The state a laptop is in after a reboot took every daemon with it. Answering with no focus rather than a made-up one is what lets the caller tell this apart from a restore that worked, and open the way it would with no saved file at all.

cases.name: a saved arrangement that never had focus
cases.why: Reachable from a file written before anything took the keyboard. The first surviving region gets it, on the same reasoning as a focused region that went: somewhere beats nowhere.
